explanation.en: A hollow (ajwaf) verb has و or ي as its middle radical: قَالَ (aslu-hu قَوَلَ), أَرَادَ (aslu-hu أَرْوَدَ). The long vowel survives before vowel-initial endings (قَالَتْ) but shortens before consonant endings (قُلْتُ) and in the jussive and imperative (لَمْ يَقُلْ، قُلْ). The Bina classifies these among the seven irregular classes (الأقسام السبعة).

examples.en: I spoke the truth and they spoke a lie — long and short stems side by side.

why.en: Before the consonant suffix ـتُ the long alif must shorten to damma: قُلْتُ.
In the jussive after لم the long vowel shortens: لم يَقُلْ.
